added_failures_note: unmeasured: the reviewed manifest names no base gate log, so the added-failure count was not taken

findings.text: follow-on: the declaration test asserts containment only (declared set contains the command modules) and does not assert each declared name resolves to a module that carries a command, so an entry that names no command could stay in CLI_MODULE_FILES unnoticed; today cli.py is such an entry -- it re-exports main from cli_entry and contributes no command callback -- and it is legitimately present as the CLI's re-export surface, so this is a gap in the guard's shape rather than a defect in this change.

item_verdicts.diff: read the three commits 32d1537ca (refactor), 9b93abe6e (test) and b52d109df (evidence) against base 1d829fe7; each carries a conventional subject and a body and no attribution trailer; the source change is 25 lines in obligation_snapshot.py and 9 in runs.py, the tuple order and the crew/*.py glob unchanged.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done-when has two clauses; the declaration test walks the click tree from cli.main and requires every top-level reckon command module to be in the tuple, and the stamp test requires both stamps to move when any declared module's bytes change and to hold when nothing does; I ran tests/test_the_cli_module_set_has_one_owner.py at head (2 passed, EXIT=0), reproduced the negative control (removing crew_follow_commands.py from the tuple makes test_every_command_module_is_declared fail naming it, EXIT=1), and reproduced the reviewer's base stamp equality exactly (old=new=follower=108721a8b90c2ba3c09be536ddcd7416e8fc9e51ecdaa82aa8b9aaa9bd5904bf over the extracted base bytes).
item_verdicts.goal: the node goal is to give the CLI's module set one owner so both code stamps read it; the diff adds CLI_MODULE_FILES to reckon/crew/obligation_snapshot.py:314 and both stamps now build their source list from it -- source_code_stamp at obligation_snapshot.py:340 and follower_code_stamp at reckon/crew/runs.py:222 -- so a CLI module named once advances a running producer and a running follower together.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it records the gate 134 passed EXIT=0 (gate.log), the negative control EXIT=1 naming crew_follow_commands.py (negative-control.log), the base stamp equality 108721a8b90c2ba3c09be536ddcd7416e8fc9e51ecdaa82aa8b9aaa9bd5904bf, and names each log on disk.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the three commits touch only reckon/crew/obligation_snapshot.py, reckon/crew/runs.py, tests/test_the_cli_module_set_has_one_owner.py and docs/evidence/fragments/every-module-fits-a-worker-window/the-cli-module-set-has-one-owner.html, all inside the manifest's declared write paths.

justifications.durability: tests/test_the_cli_module_set_has_one_owner.py:71 is a positive control asserting the click walk found modules, :74 fails naming any undeclared command module, and :121-129 assert both stamps move on an edit and restore; I confirmed the negative control fires (EXIT=1) and that the walk sees six top-level command modules.
justifications.evidence: the gate ran 134 passed EXIT=0 (gate.log), I reproduced the negative control at EXIT=1 naming crew_follow_commands.py, and I reproduced the base stamp equality 108721a8b90c2ba3c09be536ddcd7416e8fc9e51ecdaa82aa8b9aaa9bd5904bf independently from the base tree via git show.
justifications.fit: obligation_snapshot.py:305-317 states the mechanism in a comment, adds one public name and no module, and the module's imports stay stdlib-only at module level so the prompt-hook leaf constraint holds.
justifications.goal_fidelity: obligation_snapshot.py:314 declares CLI_MODULE_FILES and both obligation_snapshot.py:340 source_code_stamp and runs.py:222 follower_code_stamp build their source lists from it, so the CLI's module set has one owner and the drift the plan names cannot recur through code.
justifications.reuse: both stamps keep their existing sha256-over-source implementation and crew/*.py glob and only replace seven duplicated literals with one tuple, removing the duplication rather than adding a mechanism.
justifications.scope_discipline: the three commits change only the four declared paths (obligation_snapshot.py, runs.py, the new test file, the evidence fragment) and touch nothing outside them.
